A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same human-guided camera-scale calibration work, renamed from OfCaM to HAC. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial methodological and presentation revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original EMDB2 human and camera motion evaluations, component ablations, runtime measurements, and an appendix experiment on challenging sequences.

after.justification: V2 reports original EMDB2 and EgoBody evaluations, calibration and compatibility experiments, and supplementary analyses of depth errors and contact identification.

M1.justification: V1 combines nearest-image-keypoint depth matching with a SLAM-failure detector and GLAMR-based motion fusion. V2 replaces correspondence estimation with camera-ray/point-cloud geometry, adds human-guided ground-plane fitting for invisible contacts, and removes the failure detector and fusion procedure (Sections 4.2–4.4). The depth-ratio calibration and sequence-median aggregation remain.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates only EMDB2. V2 retains its 25 sequences and adds EgoBody, introducing head-mounted-camera footage with severe body truncation and predominantly invisible contact joints. This materially expands the evaluated input conditions.

E2.justification: V2 adds TRAM to the EMDB2 benchmark and to direct scale-calibration comparisons, alongside a ZoeDepth-fed SLAM comparator (Tables 3–5). PACE, previously compared for runtime, also receives EgoBody accuracy results. The earlier EMDB2 comparators GLAMR, TRACE, SLAHMR, and WHAM remain.

E3.justification: The default experimental configuration changes from CLIFF with DPVO to VIMO with masked DroidSLAM. V2 adds comparisons across HMR and SLAM configurations, ground-truth ground-plane and camera controls, and sequence-length groupings (Tables 2 and 4–6). The existing 100-frame human-motion alignment procedures are retained.

E4.justification: V2 removes the local-to-global fusion ablations, including v1's appendix evaluation on sequences with over 40% human occupancy. It adds ground-plane ablations, component compatibility studies, sequence-length analysis, depth-error and bias studies, and contact-identification validation with a handstand example. The existing footfall/reference-joint analysis is retained as supplementary Figure 10.

E5.justification: V2 introduces boxplots summarizing depth-error, translation-error, and signed-bias distributions (Figure 2 and supplementary Figures 7–8), adding descriptive dispersion reporting absent from v1. These concern variation within the evaluated data; neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 3's reported EMDB2 W-MPJPE/WA-MPJPE/RTE changes from 317.9/108.2/2.2 to 197.2/71.0/1.2 under the revised method and component configuration. V2 adds EgoBody results and extensive calibration results while removing fusion-specific results. Its new Table 4 also reveals a tradeoff: long-sequence ATE-S is worse than TRAM's (1.09 versus 0.80), although W-MPJPE is lower (195.30 versus 218.97). The headline changes do not isolate a same-configuration improvement.

T1.justification: V2 revises the reference-point definition to minimize point-to-ray distance and adds a ray-plane intersection formula and a coplanar-contact assumption (Sections 4.2–4.3). V1's failure-set and motion-fusion formulations disappear. The foundational camera/world transformations and scale-ratio relation remain unchanged; neither version develops theorem or proof results.

C1.justification: The contribution of adaptive local-to-global fusion for SLAM failures is replaced by ground-plane completion for out-of-view contacts and explicit claims of egocentric applicability. The abstract also changes its performance claim from 60% lower error over prior SOTA to 50% over local-to-global methods, while retaining the central optimization-free calibration claim.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations of compensation for systematic HMR depth bias, the distinction between local-pose accuracy and global-motion accuracy, and the limitations of fitting one plane on uneven terrain. V1's discussion of fusion-based recovery and EMDB-only evaluation is replaced by explicit limitations concerning catastrophic SLAM failure and long-sequence drift. Remaining errors are increasingly attributed to pose and temporal-consistency limitations.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies RANSAC ground-plane fitting, an RTX 2080 Ti for timing, metric units and RTE normalization, and use of TRAM's released HMR model. It adds a project-page address and named video/PLY resources with viewing instructions. V1's matching and failure thresholds disappear with their associated procedures. Both PDFs still promise code release upon acceptance; actual external resource availability is unverified.

R1.justification: V2 substantially develops positioning against TRAM, distinguishing foreground-human depth calibration from background metric-depth calibration. It also expands the single-view metrology discussion and references supporting human priors, ground fitting, and EgoBody. This changes the account of the closest competing approach beyond routine bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The title, method name, abstract, introduction, and substantial methodological prose are rewritten around 'Humans as Checkerboards.' Preliminaries and methods are reorganized, compatibility analysis becomes a separate subsection, limitations and conclusion are separated, and the supplement gains a structured A–E organization.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout, with extensively redrawn pipeline and calibration diagrams, new error-distribution plots, and reorganized comparison tables. Qualitative displays are revised and expanded. V1's Figure 4 moves to supplementary Figure 10, while the camera-calibration trajectory display is retained with revised examples.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens support for the central calibration idea: it measures the reliability and bias of human-depth predictions, compares directly with TRAM under component controls, and tests the new ground-plane procedure on EgoBody. These address v1's limited validation of its depth assumption and its acknowledged single-dataset coverage. Removing the SLAM-failure fallback narrows robustness, and changed default components prevent attributing headline gains solely to calibration. Nevertheless, the broader, more diagnostic evidence and clearer applicability limits provide a substantial overall quality improvement.
